sentences.text:
Sanjay Awasthi vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 January,
2020

Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh
Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 13
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 319 of 2013
Revisionist :- Sanjay Awasthi

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Revisionist :- Narendra Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the revision, including the Annexures attached
therewith.

2.  This criminal revision under Section 397/401 CrPC has been filed against the judgment and order dated 5th July, 2013 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 1, District Raebareli in Criminal Appeal No.22 of 2008, preferred by the revisionist against the judgment and order dated 27th March, 2008 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-II, Raebareli in Criminal Case No.2422 of 2007, under Section 7/16 The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'PFA Act,') and sentenced six months imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/-, and in the event of non-payment of fine, three months additional imprisonment.
3. The appellate Court has dismissed the appeal vide the impugned judgment and order dated 5th July, 2013, and affirmed the judgment of conviction and fine passed by the learned trial Court.

sentences.text: 4. The revisionist is a tea-seller; on 18.05.1999, at around 4.00 p.m., the Food Inspector found the revisionist selling 6 liter adulterated milk of buffalo and cow, without possessing valid licence; after disclosing his identity, the Food Inspector bought 750 m.l. milk; some part of the milk was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst on 19.05.1999; in his report dated 25.06.1999, the Public Analyst found the milk solids-not-fact 26% less than the prescribed limit.
5. Counsel for the revisionist submits that the milk fat was not injurious to human health; only the milk solids-not-fat was less than the prescribed limit.
The learned counsel further submits that the incident took place around 21 years before; the revisionist has undergone around 18 days imprisonment.

The learned counsel places reliance on judgment in 'Sughar Singh Vs. State and another' (Criminal Revision No.985 of 1991) in which this Court, after considering the facts of the case, which are identical to the present one, found the offence to be of very minor nature.

entities.text: Sughar Singh Vs. State and another' (Criminal Revision No.985 of 1991)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The milk solids-not-fat was not injurious to the health.

6. The Supreme Court in Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, after considering the age of the appellant in that case, and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.

entities.text: Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the said judgment of the Supreme Court, and trivial nature of the offence committed by the revisionist, it would be appropriate to reduce the sentence to the sentence already undergone by the revisionist with enhanced fine.

8. In view thereof, the sentence awarded to the revisionist is reduced to the sentence already undergone by him with fine of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) to be deposited by the revisionist with the 'Army Battle Casualty Welfare Fund, New Delhi' within a period of four weeks from today.

entities.text: Army Battle Casualty Welfare Fund, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
9. Thus, the revision is allowed partly.
10.
Let copy of this order, along with lower court record, be sent to the concerned Court below forthwith for compliance.

[D.K. Singh, J.] Order Date :- 22.1.2020 MVS/-

6. The Supreme Court in Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, after considering the age of the appellant in that case, and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.
